This may lead to a less comprehensive review. ## Walkthrough Removed `deleterange_concurrency` from the TiKV configuration scaffold and introduced a commented `batchdelete_count`. TiKV store now batches explicit per-key deletions (controlled by `batchCommitSize`) and propagates `context.Context` through transaction APIs, replacing implicit range-delete operations. ## Changes | Cohort / File(s) | Change Summary | |---|---| | **Configuration Update**
`weed/command/scaffold/filer.toml` | Removed `deleterange_concurrency` under `[tikv]`; added a commented `batchdelete_count` option with descriptive comment lines. | | **TiKV store core & batching**
`weed/filer/tikv/tikv_store.go` | Added `defaultBatchCommitSize = 10000` and `batchCommitSize` field on `TikvStore`. Initialize reads `batchdelete_count`. Replaced range-delete logic with iterator-based accumulation and batched explicit deletes via new `deleteBatch(ctx, keys)` helper. Updated DeleteFolderChildren to stream keys and delete in batches. | | **Transaction wrapper & context propagation**
`weed/filer/tikv/tikv_store.go` | Changed `TxnWrapper.RunInTxn` signature to `RunInTxn(ctx context.Context, f func(txn *txnkv.KVTxn) error) error`. RunInTxn now commits using provided ctx for implicit transactions and rolls back on error. getTxn/Begin/Commit/Rollback flows adjusted to use context where appropriate. | | **KV operations context forwarding**
`weed/filer/tikv/tikv_store_kv.go` | Propagated `context.Context` into all `RunInTxn` invocations for KvPut, KvGet, and KvDelete (e.g., `tw.RunInTxn(ctx, ...)`). No other logic changes. | ## Sequence Diagram(s) ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Client participant TikvStore participant TxnWrapper participant KVTxn as KVTxn (TiKV) rect rgb(255, 244, 230) note over Client,KVTxn: Old flow — range delete (removed) Client->>TikvStore: DeleteFolderChildren(prefix) TikvStore->>TxnWrapper: RunInTxn(handler) TxnWrapper->>KVTxn: Begin() KVTxn->>KVTxn: DeleteRange(prefix) --(could affect unrelated rawkv keys) KVTxn->>TxnWrapper: OK TxnWrapper->>KVTxn: Commit() end rect rgb(235, 250, 255) note over Client,KVTxn: New flow — context-aware batched deletes Client->>TikvStore: DeleteFolderChildren(ctx, prefix) TikvStore->>TxnWrapper: RunInTxn(ctx, handler) TxnWrapper->>KVTxn: Begin() loop iterate keys with iterator KVTxn-->>TxnWrapper: next key TxnWrapper->>TikvStore: accumulate key alt batch full or iteration finished TikvStore->>TxnWrapper: deleteBatch(ctx, keys) TxnWrapper->>KVTxn: Delete(key1)...Delete(keyN) KVTxn-->>TxnWrapper: OK end end TxnWrapper->>KVTxn: Commit(ctx) end ``` ## Estimated code review effort 🎯 4 (Complex) | ⏱️ ~50 minutes - Attention areas: - Correctness of batch accumulation and that no keys are skipped or duplicated in DeleteFolderChildren. - deleteBatch transaction semantics: commit vs. rollback behavior when transactions are implicit vs. user-provided. - Proper propagation and use of ctx through TxnWrapper, getTxn, Begin/Commit/Rollback and all RunInTxn call sites. - Interaction with external rawkv clients and ensuring new per-key deletes do not regress concurrency or performance. ## Poem > 🐰 > Batch by batch I nibble through the rows, > No sweeping ranges where the wild wind blows. > Each key a carrot, checked before it's gone, > Context in paw, I hop the whole night long. > Safe burrows now — deletions hop along. ## Pre-merge checks and finishing touches

# Transforming Code Reviews with AI

## Features

**Automated Reviews**: Continuous reviews of the pull requests including incremental commits. 

**Summarization**: Generates high-level summary and a technical walkthrough of the PR changes. 

**Line-by-line review**: Provides line-by-line suggestions committable with one click.

**Codebase verification**:  Verifies the impact on the overall codebase and identifies missing changes.

**Insights into your code**:  Ask any questions on your codebase within the pull request 

**Chat about your code** : Chat with the bot around your code. The more you chat, the smarter it gets.

**Issue Validation**:  Validates the PR against the linked issues and identifies other related issues

## Summary of Changes Hello @chrislusf, I'm Gemini Code Assist[^1]! I'm currently reviewing this pull request and will post my feedback shortly. In the meantime, here's a summary to help you and other reviewers quickly get up to speed! This pull request resolves a critical data integrity issue in the TiKV filer where batch deletions could inadvertently corrupt data belonging to other services. By transitioning from a RawKV `DeleteRange` operation to a transaction-based batch deletion approach, the system now guarantees proper transaction isolation and prevents accidental data loss, ensuring that operations respect TiKV's MVCC and maintain distinct logical keyspaces for transactional and RawKV clients. ### Highlights * **Problem Solved**: Addressed a critical bug where TiKV's `DeleteRange` (a RawKV operation) could accidentally delete KV pairs from other services using the RawKV client when the filer used a transaction client, leading to data corruption. * **Solution Implemented**: Replaced the problematic `client.DeleteRange()` with transactional batch deletes using `txn.Delete()` to ensure transaction isolation, respect TiKV's MVCC, and prevent accidental data loss. * **Batch Processing**: Introduced configurable batching for deletes (default 10,000 keys per transaction) to manage memory and transaction size limits effectively, improving performance and reliability. * **Context Propagation**: Enhanced `RunInTxn` to accept and propagate `context.Context`, enabling proper timeout and cancellation handling across various operations. * **Key Copying**: Ensured proper key copying (`append([]byte(nil), key...)`) during iteration to prevent issues arising from iterator buffer reuse, which could lead to incorrect deletions. * **Configuration Update**: Replaced the `deleterange_concurrency` configuration option with `batchdelete_count` in `filer.toml` to support the new transactional batch deletion mechanism.
Using Gemini Code Assist
The full guide for Gemini Code Assist can be found on our [documentation page](https://developers.google.com/gemini-code-assist/docs/review-github-code), here are some quick tips. Invoking Gemini You can request assistance from Gemini at any point by creating a comment using either `/gemini ` or `@gemini-code-assist `. Below is a summary of the supported commands on the current page. Feature | Command | Description --- | --- | --- Code Review | `/gemini review` | Performs a code review for the current pull request in its current state. Pull Request Summary | `/gemini summary` | Provides a summary of the current pull request in its current state. Comment | @gemini-code-assist | Responds in comments when explicitly tagged, both in pull request comments and review comments. Help | `/gemini help` | Displays a list of available commands. Customization To customize Gemini Code Assist for GitHub experience, repository maintainers can create a configuration file and/or provide a custom code review style guide (such as PEP-8 for Python) by creating and adding files to a `.gemini/` folder in the base of the repository. Detailed instructions can be found [here](https://developers.google.com/gemini-code-assist/docs/customize-gemini-behavior-github). Limitations & Feedback Gemini Code Assist may make mistakes. Please leave feedback on any instances where its feedback is incorrect or counter productive. You can react with :thumbsup: and :thumbsdown: on @gemini-code-assist comments. If you're interested in giving your feedback about your experience with Gemini Code Assist for Github and other Google products, sign up [here](https://google.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_2cyuGuTWsEw84yG). You can also get AI-powered code generation, chat, as well as code reviews directly in the IDE at no cost with the [Gemini Code Assist IDE Extension](https://cloud.google.com/products/gemini/code-assist).
